Lightning
līt´ning
n. (a flash from heaven; rendering Hebrew baraq, Greek astrape)
From lighten, to flash. Scripture's interest is in its speed and its universal visibility — both of which it makes theological.

Biblical Definition

Lightning is the sudden flash of heaven. Christ uses it for the manner of His return, ruling out any secret or local arrival: “For as the lightning cometh out of the east, and shineth even unto the west; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be” (Mat 24:27). He uses it again for Satan's fall (Luk 10:18). Sinai is described by it (Exo 19:16), the throne in Revelation issues it (Rev 4:5), and the angel at the tomb had a countenance “like lightning” (Mat 28:3).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines lightning as a sudden discharge of electricity from a cloud, or from the earth to a cloud, which produces a vivid flash of light.

expand to see more

LIGHTNING, n. A sudden discharge of electricity from a cloud to the earth, or from the earth to a cloud, or from one cloud to another, producing a vivid flash of light.

2. A sudden brightness; as the lightning of the countenance.

Key Scripture

Mat 24:27 — "For as the lightning cometh out of the east, and shineth even unto the west; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be."

Luk 10:18 — "And he said unto them, I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven."

Exo 19:16 — "And it came to pass on the third day in the morning, that there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud upon the mount, and the voice of the trumpet exceeding loud; so that all the people that was in the camp trembled."

Rev 4:5 — "And out of the throne proceeded lightnings and thunderings and voices: and there were seven lamps of fire burning before the throne, which are the seven Spirits of God."

Modern Corruption

Every private claim that Christ has secretly returned, or is present in one place with one group, is refuted by the single simile He chose — lightning is seen by everyone at once.

expand to see more

Matthew 24 sets the simile inside a warning about exactly this error. If they shall say unto you, Behold, he is in the desert; go not forth: behold, he is in the secret chambers; believe it not. For as the lightning cometh out of the east, and shineth even unto the west; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be. The comparison functions as a test: any return that requires an insider to point it out is not the one Christ described.

Luke 10:18 shows the other direction of the flash. I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven — spoken to seventy ordinary disciples returning from a mission, astonished that even the devils were subject to them. The fall was as sudden and as visible from above as the coming will be from below, and Christ's next word keeps them from pride: rejoice not that the spirits are subject unto you, but rather rejoice, because your names are written in heaven.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew baraq (H1300), lightning, a flash — also used of a glittering sword; Greek astrape (G796), lightning, brightness.

expand to see more

Hebrew baraq (H1300) — lightning; Exodus 19:16, Psalm 97:4, his lightnings enlightened the world.

Greek astrape (G796) — lightning, bright shining; Matthew 24:27, Luke 10:18, 17:24.

Hebrew chaziz (H2385) — a flash, thunderbolt; Job 28:26, a way for the lightning of the thunder.

Usage

"“As the lightning cometh out of the east, and shineth even unto the west” — nothing secret about it."

"“I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven” — the fall was as sudden as the coming."

"“His countenance was like lightning” — the angel at the empty tomb."
